scope: Second fixed scalar cost experiment, using byte-identical probes and the same persistent-cache baseline as the first trial.
qualification: 869 all-feature scalar library results, 28 doctests, strict release all-feature all-target Clippy, warning-denied docs and formatting pass. All fixed cost processes succeed and all mathematical witnesses and representation inventories agree within each suite/mode.
result: Affine and pi-transport quadratic queries become faster and allocate less, but mixed-field declines are slower in all five pairs (median ratios about 1.582 first/warm and 1.349 cloned), with 18000 additional allocation calls per 1000 inputs. Conjugate-then-affine warm/cloned queries also regress in all five pairs. Native gates are not advanced for this rejected source.
time_limits: Several rational-suite timing pairs have large process-wide variation. All samples remain included; there is no selective resampling or statistical significance claim. The mixed-field allocation increase and consistent paired timing regression are sufficient to reject this version.
inspection_correction: v3-inspection-correction.json notes that the removed zero field shared a static Rational and did not itself allocate. Repeated exact Int-leaf conversion remains a separate optimization hypothesis.
next_step: Evaluate existing canonical small-rational reuse at Computable::exact_rational integer leaves against the frozen persistent-cache baseline, without either rejected direct traversal. Include integer width controls and retain all original cache fallback tests before any native gate.
